newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse surrenders to international trend.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse surrenders to international trend.

text.p: A price fall on the Budapest Stock Exchange accelerated in early trading on Friday in what traders said was the result of a tumble on Wall Street.
But traders said the market was in a downward corrective phase and the Dow's fall just reinforced the trend.
"The fall on Wall Street has strengthened the correction," one trader said.

The Budapest Stock Exchange has been on a downward path since last Friday, interrupted only by a less than one percent rise on Wednesday. By the end of trade on Thursday, the BUX index lost nearly five percent.
On Friday the market's leading stocks were heavy losers.
At 1047 GMT chemicals TVK traded at 1,970 forints, down 80.
The market's other chemicals stock, Borsodchem, rated by Hungary's Postabank Securities as 'buy', suffered smaller losses and at 1049 GMT traded at 5,870, down 130.
Heavy losers also included hotelier Danubius which traded at 4,550 forints, down 205, at 1051 GMT, and some of the pharmaceuticals stocks, too.
At 1050 GMT Richter traded at 10,825 forints, down 385. Human stood at 2,800 forints, down 100, at 1048 GMT.
Tile maker Zalakeramia, which announced its second acquisition since the end of February, has dipped only 50 forints in one deal so far to 8,150.
